# Welcome {background-color="#275882"}

## Welcome to PS50008A! {.center}

**Research Methods & Experimental Design**

Your first session of the module

---

## Today: DataLab

::: {.objectives-box}
**Today You Will:**

- Complete Part 1 of the survey (mood, personality, demographics)
- Rotate through 6 cognitive task stations
- Record your data in Qualtrics
- Complete Part 2 of the survey (mood again!)
- Form your project groups
:::

---

## Why DataLab?

The data you generate today becomes our teaching dataset for the term.

When we learn about:

- Distributions → [your reaction times]{.hl-yellow}
- t-tests → [Lab A vs Lab B]{.hl-blue}
- Correlations → [personality × performance]{.hl-green}
- Pre-post designs → [your mood change]{.hl-yellow}

...we'll use **your** data.

# How It Works {background-color="#275882"}

## The Process

::: {.incremental}
1. Collect your participant card and note your group colour
2. Complete **Part 1** of the Qualtrics survey
3. Go to your assigned starting station
4. Complete the task with your partner
5. Enter your data in Qualtrics
6. Move to next station when the bell rings
7. Complete **Part 2** of the survey at the end
:::

---

## Recording Your Data

::: {.callout-important}
## This is Real Research!
Record data carefully—your data will be used throughout the term.
:::

- Use the Qualtrics link on your phone/laptop
- Enter your participant ID (from your card)
- Follow the instructions at each station
- Complete station data entry BEFORE moving on

---

## Timing

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 0:00-0:15 | Welcome, Part 1 survey, form groups |
| 0:15-1:45 | Station rotations (~12-15 min each) |
| 1:45-1:55 | Part 2 survey |
| 1:55-2:00 | Debrief & wrap-up |

---

# The Pre-Post Design {background-color="#275882"}

## Measuring Change

We're measuring your mood, energy, and stress **twice**:

- **Before** the stations (Part 1)
- **After** the stations (Part 2)

This lets us analyse whether DataLab affected how you feel!

::: {.callout-note}
## Within-Subjects Design
Each person serves as their own control — we compare your "before" to your "after."
:::

---

# Project Groups {background-color="#275882"}

## Form Your Groups

By the end of today, form groups of [**3-4 students**]{.inverse-box}.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Consider:
- Can you meet outside class?
- Will you be reliable partners?
- You'll work together all term
:::

---

## What Groups Do

Your group will:

- Work together on the **group research project**
- Conduct labs together from **Week 16**
- Generate data for the **Research Report** (Week 22)

# Station Previews {background-color="#275882"}

## Station 1: Reflex Test

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/station1-reflex.png)
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**How fast is your nervous system?**

- Partner drops a ruler without warning
- You catch it as fast as possible
- The distance = your reaction time (physics!)
- 5 trials each
:::
::::

---

## Station 2: Mind Palace

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/station2-mind-palace.png)
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**What survives the interference?**

- Study 10 words (30 seconds)
- Do maths problems (60 seconds)
- Recall as many words as you can
- Which positions did you remember?
:::
::::

---

## Station 3: Time Warp

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/station3-time-warp.png)
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Your brain's internal clock**

- Estimate when 60 seconds have passed
- Estimate the length of lines (visual)
- Estimate the length of strings (touch only!)
:::
::::

---

## Station 4: Sixth Sense

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/station4-sixth-sense.png)
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Can you detect being watched?**

- Sit back-to-back with partner
- Partner randomly stares or looks away
- Can you tell which? How confident are you?
- 6 trials each
:::
::::

---

## Station 5: Lady Luck

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/station5-lady-luck.png)
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**How "random" can you be?**

- Generate 20 random numbers (1-10)
- Roll dice 10 times
- Flip coins 10 times
- Are humans good at being random?
:::
::::

---

## Station 6: Frontal Lob

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](images/station6-frontal-lob.png)
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**Precision meets confidence**

- Rate your throwing ability (1-10)
- Throw ping pong balls at a basket
- How well did you predict your performance?
- This is called **calibration**
:::
::::

---
